response:
Reflection on gen-4: a sharp regularity has emerged across 28 evaluated signals. **Downside-state and level conditioners work; trend and change conditioners do not.** The two new floor conditioners both delivered (margin floor α 5.4% t 4.38; pre-research earnings floor α 5.4% t 3.52, Sharpe 0.52), while every dynamic conditioner tested — runway trend (α 1.3%), margin erosion from peak (α 2.2%), ΔR&D intensity (α 1.3%), productivity trend (α −1.7%) — produced strong FMB slopes but negligible or negative alpha, meaning the changes are cross-sectionally informative but not tradable in tails. Symmetric volatility conditioners are also weak (revenue-growth VOL α 1.5%) while asymmetric downside statistics on the same variable family are strong, and the advertiser-only test failed outright (α −0.7%, coverage 0.059), closing the brand channel. The best single result remains cash × R&D intensity (α 6.9%, t 5.26). This batch therefore systematically extends the *floor* family to the two variables it has not touched (research commitment and demand), converts the best conditioner from a point-in-time level to a worst-case level, introduces a genuinely different aggregation rule (weakest-link MIN rather than rank stacking), and tests one new economic channel plus one new value-leg construction.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Never-Dry Innovator Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(che, at), 5), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: What insures an unpledgeable research program is not the cash balance today but the fact that the firm has never run its buffer down: an innovator whose worst cash-to-assets level over five years is still comfortable has demonstrated it can fund research through a full cycle without external capital, whereas today's cash pile at a firm that has been empty before offers no such assurance.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's strongest alpha comes from cash × R&D intensity, and the archive's strongest new conditioners are worst-case states rather than current levels, so replacing the point-in-time buffer with its five-year minimum is a substantive test of whether funding *security* rather than funding *level* is the priced attribute. It is not a variable substitution but a change in the statistic's economic content, and it should also stabilize portfolio membership because a five-year minimum turns over far less than a current ratio.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Sustained Research Commitment Floor
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Knowledge capital is built by the research a firm never cuts; the minimum R&D intensity sustained across five years measures the committed, contractual core of the program, whereas average intensity is inflated by opportunistic spikes that create little durable capital, so cheapness combined with a high research floor identifies undervalued firms whose knowledge stock is real.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Floors have been the archive's most productive conditioner form, but they have only been applied to profits and margins; applying the same downside logic to intangible investment itself is the natural untested case, and it is economically distinct from both mean intensity (which the peer-relative signals used) and from smoothness (whose CV form produced only α 2.1%). Firms with no research get a floor of exactly zero, which correctly places them at the bottom of the conditioner without creating a spurious tie at the favorable end.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cheap With a Demand Floor
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), WINSOR(TS_MIN(GROWTH(revt, 1), 5), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Customer capital shows up not as smooth revenue but as revenue that does not collapse: a firm whose worst annual revenue change over five years is mild has an installed base and switching costs protecting its demand, while a firm that has suffered a sharp revenue contraction has no such unrecorded asset regardless of how volatile its growth is on average.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This directly repairs the gen-4 customer-demand signal, whose symmetric volatility conditioner earned only α 1.5% (t 1.23) because it penalized firms with rapid upside growth as heavily as those with demand collapses. Replacing the two-sided volatility with the one-sided worst-case growth aligns the demand channel with the asymmetric statistic that has worked twice already on margins and profits, and it isolates whether the earlier weakness was the channel or the statistic.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Weakest-Link Reliability Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), MIN(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5)), RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1)))))))
HYPOTHESIS: A cheap intangible-intensive firm is only safe if it fails on none of its reliability dimensions — funding, pricing power, and book integrity — so the informative summary is the firm's *binding constraint*, the worst of its three conditioner ranks, not their average; averaging lets a spectacular cash balance excuse a commodity margin or an acquisition-inflated book.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every prior multi-channel attempt used additive rank stacking, which the critic rightly called reweighting; the minimum operator is a different aggregation rule with its own economic claim (survival is conjunctive, not compensatory) and produces a genuinely different firm ordering, concentrating the long leg on firms that are adequate everywhere rather than extreme somewhere. If the weakest-link form beats the additive composites, the search should aggregate conjunctively from here; if it does not, the reliability channels are substitutes and future effort should focus on one channel measured well.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cheap Asset-Light Franchise
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(at, ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), che)), revt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: When a firm produces a given level of revenue with very little hard operating capital — assets net of purchased intangibles and cash — the output must be coming from unrecorded organizational and knowledge capital; such a firm's book value understates its economic capital most severely, so its cheapness on reported earnings is the most likely to be mismeasurement rather than distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a new economic channel: rather than asking whether the recorded book is reliable or the margin durable, it infers the *existence* of off-balance-sheet capital from the gap between revenue generated and hard capital employed. Netting out both purchased intangibles and cash from the asset base is essential and distinguishes it from a standard asset-turnover quality screen, because it isolates tangible operating capital as the denominator rather than the accounting total.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Cyclically-Normalized Innovator Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0), ), 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Single-year pre-research earnings are a noisy estimate of an innovator's earning power because research programs and product cycles are lumpy; averaging pre-R&D earnings over five years before dividing by today's price yields a cyclically normalized yield that measures cheapness against sustainable earning power rather than against a transient print.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every strong signal in the archive shares the same point-in-time value leg, so the leg itself has never been tested as a design choice even though the evidence overwhelmingly favors smoothed and worst-case fundamentals over instantaneous ones on the conditioner side. Pairing the normalized yield with the archive's best conditioner holds the conditioner fixed, so any change in alpha is cleanly attributable to the value construction, and normalization should also reduce the turnover that currently comes from earnings volatility.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Never-Dry Innovator Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a one-operator substitution inside the archive's already-tested best signal (Cash-Insured Innovation Value), and because cash-to-assets is highly persistent the five-year minimum will be nearly collinear with the current level, so the "funding security vs. funding level" distinction it claims to test is unlikely to be identifiable.

---CRITIQUE Sustained Research Commitment Floor---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: R&D intensity is one of the most persistent firm characteristics, so TS_MIN(xrd/at,5) is effectively a proxy for the R&D-intensity level already used in several archive signals (and mostly just separates R&D from non-R&D firms via the zero floor), making this a near-rediscovery of value × R&D intensity rather than a new economic statistic.

---CRITIQUE Cheap With a Demand Floor---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The one-sided worst-case revenue-growth conditioner is internally consistent with the stated sign and is a genuine diagnostic repair of the failed two-sided volatility version, though it overlaps meaningfully with fundamental-volatility/distress screens and worst-case revenue contraction may proxy for realized bad news rather than absent customer capital.

---CRITIQUE Weakest-Link Reliability Value---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The minimum-of-ranks aggregation is a substantively different (conjunctive rather than compensatory) combination rule with a falsifiable economic claim and clear interpretation either way, and the expression's direction is consistent with the positive expected sign, despite the mild kitchen-sink risk of stacking three previously tested conditioners.

---CRITIQUE Cheap Asset-Light Franchise---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Netting cash and purchased intangibles out of assets leaves what is essentially tangible asset turnover, so this reduces to the well-known value × asset-turnover (DuPont/quality) composite rather than a new inference about off-balance-sheet capital, and the revt denominator is fragile for low-revenue firms even after winsorization.

---CRITIQUE Cyclically-Normalized Innovator Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The expression is malformed (trailing comma in `ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0), )`), and the core idea — a multi-year average earnings numerator over current price — is the long-documented cyclically-adjusted/normalized earnings-yield anomaly bolted onto the archive's existing best conditioner, so both the construction and the novelty are weak.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Refinancing Cliff Risk for Innovators
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, ADD(che, dlc)), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A research-intensive firm fails not when its cash is low but when maturing obligations arrive before its research pays off; the share of near-term liabilities not covered by cash measures a funding cliff that must be met by asset sales or dilution precisely because knowledge capital cannot be pledged, so cheap innovators without a cliff are undervalued and those with one are correctly discounted.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This abandons the persistent cash-level statistic the critic showed would be collinear with its own five-year minimum, and instead uses the maturity structure of debt — `dlc` relative to the cash available to retire it — which no archive signal has touched and which varies for reasons (refinancing calendars, credit-line draws) largely independent of the cash-to-assets level. The ratio is bounded in [0,1] with a well-behaved denominator, equals zero for firms with no current debt, and is gated by R&D intensity so the funding-cliff interpretation applies only to firms running an unpledgeable investment program.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Knowledge Stock Vintage Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), COALESCE(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 2), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: Knowledge capital depreciates quickly, so two firms with identical R&D stocks differ economically depending on vintage: one whose stock is concentrated in the last two years owns current-generation technology, while one whose stock is mostly five years old holds capital that capitalization schedules overstate and competitors have already imitated.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The critic is right that a floor on R&D intensity is just the persistent intensity level in disguise; vintage share is a *composition* statistic that is deliberately scale-free — it is invariant to how much a firm spends and varies only with the time profile of that spending, so it cannot proxy for intensity or for the R&D-versus-no-R&D split. Non-reporting firms have an undefined ratio and are assigned zero, which is the economically correct reading (no fresh knowledge) rather than a coverage patch.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Replacement-Cost Cheapness of Knowledge Capital
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che)), NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: The economic capital a buyer would have to reproduce is tangible assets plus accumulated knowledge capital, excluding purchased intangibles that reflect past transaction prices rather than reproduction cost; when enterprise value sits far below that reproduction cost, the market is refusing to pay for capital that demonstrably exists.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This replaces the turnover-in-disguise construction with a genuine valuation anchor the archive lacks — a replacement-cost (inverse-Q) numerator rather than an earnings, sales, or realizable-asset numerator — and it avoids the fragile low-revenue denominator by dividing by enterprise value, which is bounded away from zero for essentially all firms. Pairing it with the already-validated peer-excess soft-book conditioner holds the conditioner fixed, so the evaluation isolates the new anchor's contribution.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Trough Pre-Research Earnings Cheapness
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_MIN(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A value signal should ask whether a firm is cheap against the earnings it produces in its worst year, not its most recent or its average year; for intangible-intensive firms whose reported earnings are depressed by expensed research and lumpy product cycles, trough pre-R&D earnings relative to price is the conservative measure of what the buyer is guaranteed.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The malformed averaging construction is replaced by a downside statistic, which is the transformation the archive has shown to work repeatedly on conditioners (margin floor α 5.4%, pre-research earnings floor α 5.4%) but which has never been applied to the value leg itself — and it is explicitly not the published cyclically-adjusted average earnings yield, since a trough and a mean rank firms very differently when earnings are skewed. Holding the conditioner identical to Signal 3 makes the two proposals a clean head-to-head on which new valuation anchor carries more information.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
